title: Geometric (cis/trans) Isomers

titles.subject: Chemistry
titles.chapter: An Introduction to AS Level Organic Chemistry

author: oA7a2DXCeN3DLamvj
chapter_outcomes: define the term hydrocarbon as a compound made up of C and H atoms only
understand that alkanes are simple hydrocarbons with no functional group
understand that the compounds in the syllabus contain a functional group which dictates their physical and chemical properties
interpret and use the general, structural, displayed and skeletal formulas of the classes of compound stated in the table on pages 29 and 30 (syllabus)

understand and use systematic nomenclature of simple aliphatic organic molecules with functional groups detailed in the table on pages 29 and 30, up to six carbon atoms (six plus six for esters, straight chains only for esters and nitriles)
deduce the molecular and/or empirical formula of a compound, given its structural, displayed or skeletal formula

Students will be able to identify and classify organic molecules by interpreting homologous series and distinguishing between saturated and unsaturated structures. They must also define the nature of bond breaking through homolytic and heterolytic fission, and describe the behavior of free radicals throughout the three stages of a chain reaction: initiation, propagation, and termination.

Learners will categorize chemical species as nucleophiles (electron-pair donors) or electrophiles (electron-pair acceptors) to determine if a reaction is nucleophilic or electrophilic in nature. Furthermore, students must be able to distinguish between broad reaction types, including addition, substitution, elimination, hydrolysis, and condensation, while using $[O]$ and $[H]$ to represent oxidation and reduction in organic redox equations.

Students will describe and illustrate specific reaction pathways, including free-radical substitution, electrophilic addition, nucleophilic substitution, and nucleophilic addition. To demonstrate this understanding, they must correctly apply the use of curly arrows to represent the movement of electron pairs, ensuring each arrow starts precisely at a bond or lone pair.
describe organic molecules as either straight-chained, branched or cyclic
describe and explain the shape of, and bond angles in, molecules containing $\mathrm{sp, sp^2}$ and $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridised atoms
describe the arrangement of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds in molecules containing  $\mathrm{sp, sp^2}$ and $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridised atoms
understand and use the term planar when describing the arrangement of atoms in organic molecules, for example ethene
describe structural isomerism and its division into chain, positional and functional group isomerism
describe stereoisomerism and its division into geometrical (cis/trans) and optical isomerism
describe geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism in alkenes, and explain its origin in terms of restricted rotation due to the presence of $\pi$ bonds
explain what is meant by a chiral centre and that such a centre gives rise to two optical isomers (enantiomers)
identify chiral centres and geometrical (cis/trans) isomerism in a molecule of given structural formula including cyclic compounds
deduce the possible isomers for an organic molecule of known molecular formula
